findings.title: Converting cyclic Markdown drawings can crash the host process
findings.summary: A Markdown image with a `drawing:` payload can provide a self-referential dependency index. `markdown_to_docx()` accepts the decoded graph and `dep_part()` recurses without cycle or depth checks, exhausting the process stack before returning an error.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reliably deny availability of the conversion process through the public default parser boundary. No privileges, network exposure or deployment were assumed; impact is process availability rather than code execution or disclosure.
severity.changeConditions: A shared remotely reachable conversion deployment would increase operational impact; process isolation limits blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Parent source trace confirms direct deserialization, public conversion dispatch and unconditional recursive self-index traversal. No runtime reproduction was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Markdown parser accepts drawing payload
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-controlled image destination is decoded and retained as a Drawing with no dependency-graph validation.

codeEvidence.label: Payload JSON defines dependency references
codeEvidence.explanation: Base64 decoding and serde deserialization preserve caller-supplied part indexes.

codeEvidence.label: Package writer materializes the payload
codeEvidence.explanation: The accepted drawing is passed to materialize during package assembly.

codeEvidence.label: Root relationships enter dependent parts
codeEvidence.explanation: A root part index within bounds starts traversal of the same dependency array.

codeEvidence.label: Recursive materializer lacks cycle tracking
codeEvidence.explanation: A dependency relationship pointing to its own index passes the length check and recurses before producing a part. used tracks output names, not visited indexes.

codeEvidence.label: Capture memoizes before recursion
codeEvidence.explanation: The DOCX capture side tracks indexes, unlike the inverse materializer; its count cap does not make the graph acyclic.

rootCause.summary: `picture()` accepts the image destination as an encoded `Drawing`; `decode()` performs only base64/JSON decoding, preserving arbitrary `rels[].part` indexes. Package assembly calls `materialize()`, which enters `dep_part()` for any in-range root index. Each dependent relation invokes `dep_part()` again for any in-range child index without an in-progress set or depth bound. A child pointing back to index zero therefore recurses forever; the `used` set only renames parts and cannot break the cycle.

findings.remediation: Validate the decoded dependency graph before materialization; track in-progress and completed dependency indexes, reject cycles and enforce depth/work budgets, and memoize each completed part for shared DAGs.

counterEvidence: Capture uses a memoized index and caps dependent parts/relations, but decode/materialize do not enforce acyclicity; a one-node graph fits all count limits.
Package part equality is checked only after recursive traversal; it cannot stop self-reference.
limitations: No application execution or crash reproduction; no remote service deployment established.
validation.summary: A flat JSON envelope with one root relation to dependency zero and dependency zero relating to itself passes the only index bounds checks. Recursive descent occurs before base64/XML output or deduplication, so even a small input reaches nonterminating recursion. Capture limits and serde JSON nesting limits do not constrain a cycle represented as flat integer indexes.

dataflow.summary: Markdown image -> picture() -> decode() -> package drawing() -> materialize() -> recursive dep_part()
dataflow.outcome: Stack exhaustion terminates or traps the calling process/runtime

impact.why: Loss of conversion-process availability; no source-supported confidentiality or execution gain.

likelihood.why: A single small self-referential graph passes in-range checks under the default public API.

reachability.summary: Any caller processing supplier-controlled Markdown through `markdown_to_docx()` reaches this path without special flags or operator configuration.
reachability.outcome: Denial of service in the caller process
preconditions: The victim converts attacker-supplied Markdown containing the supported drawing payload syntax.

attackPath.summary: Supply a Markdown image whose URL-safe base64 `drawing:` JSON has root `part:0` and `deps[0].rels[0].part:0`; invoke the default public Markdown-to-DOCX conversion.

remediationTests: Convert a self-cycle and a two-node cycle and assert a typed refusal without recursion.
Convert a deeply nested chain and a shared-dependency DAG under bounded work and ensure valid parts retain expected identity.

baselineCounterEvidence: MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES constrain capture, not decode; a single-node cycle fits.
Nested drawing/text-box XML checks do not validate dependency cycles.
Malformed JSON refuses safely; cyclic envelope uses valid flat JSON.

findings.title: Converting a compact legacy DOC can exhaust memory through aliased text pieces
findings.summary: Legacy DOC piece records can map many increasing logical character ranges onto the same physical text bytes. `main_text()` materializes every logical character into an unbudgeted `StoryChar` vector, allowing a small file to consume many gigabytes before DOCX admission.

severity.rationale: The public legacy parser accepts supplier-controlled files and permits predictable memory/CPU amplification without privileged settings. Impact is availability of the caller process; no remote service or broader compromise was established.
severity.changeConditions: A shared exposed conversion service would increase blast radius; enforced worker memory/CPU limits constrain host impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent baseline and focused investigation plus parent review establish that valid increasing CPs and repeated in-bounds FC ranges pass existing checks. Memory thresholds were not dynamically measured.

codeEvidence.label: CLI converts legacy input before DOCX admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Legacy conversion invokes the vulnerable public reader before later package parsing.

codeEvidence.label: Logical CP ordering is enforced
codeEvidence.explanation: This rejects repeated/decreasing logical ranges but permits contiguous increasing ranges sharing physical backing.

rootCause.summary: The FIB supplies `ccp_text` and each PCD supplies a physical `fc`. CP endpoints must be contiguous and increasing, but multiple PCDs can select the same physical byte range. `main_text()` calculates each byte offset relative to that PCD and appends one retained `StoryChar` per logical CP. No logical-character, output-allocation or expansion-work budget is checked before the vector grows; bounds on physical streams do not bound repeated references.

findings.remediation: Enforce explicit legacy logical-character, piece-count and expanded-memory/work budgets before constructing StoryChar values; retain legitimate physical aliases only within that budget and return a typed refusal through every public legacy API.

counterEvidence: Sector chains are bounded and repeated FAT locations rejected; integer arithmetic and physical byte reads are checked.
Decreasing CPs and gaps are refused, so the rejected repeated 0..N logical-range proposal is not needed. This construction uses increasing contiguous CPs.
The repository recommends host process limits, which constrain damage but do not provide a bounded parser refusal.
limitations: No application execution, exploit fixture or memory threshold measurement; no deployment exposure assumed.
validation.method: Independent offline source trace and arithmetic construction
validation.summary: For example, 10,000 compressed pieces can describe successive 65,536-character CP ranges while all choose the same 64 KiB physical text. `ccp_text=655360000` is within u32; the approximately 120 KB piece table and backing bytes remain compact, all CP and byte checks pass, and the loop requests 655 million character records. The public reader and legacy CLI reach expansion before subsequent package checks.

findings.title: Rendering an admitted DOCX can retain gigabytes of duplicate embedded fonts
findings.summary: Distinct font-table aliases may all reference one embedded font part. Rendering eagerly loads every alias, copies the full font and retains a separate buffer for each name, multiplying a small admitted package into gigabytes of memory even if its body never uses those fonts.

severity.rationale: A supplier-controlled DOCX crosses the public renderer boundary under ordinary options and predictably exhausts caller memory. Source establishes process availability impact, without assuming a remote deployment or confidentiality/code-execution gain.
severity.changeConditions: Shared conversion services have greater availability impact; isolated memory-limited workers constrain host damage.

confidence.rationale: Parent review confirms unconditional loading, bytes.to_vec() per alias and distinct retained map entries. Exact exhaustion thresholds were not executed.

taxonomy.category: Unbounded expansion of shared embedded resources

codeEvidence.label: Renderer eagerly loads all embedded fonts
codeEvidence.explanation: Ordinary DOCX rendering first admits physical package bytes.

codeEvidence.label: All font table entries are loaded before run selection
codeEvidence.explanation: All embedded rows load regardless of whether body runs reference their names.

codeEvidence.label: Document supplies distinct font aliases and embedding IDs
codeEvidence.explanation: Each attacker-controlled font name and r:id creates an independent table entry.

codeEvidence.label: Deobfuscation always copies the full part
codeEvidence.explanation: Even an already plain TTF is copied before header detection; the copy is not shared by part identity.

codeEvidence.label: Every alias retains its own decoded font buffer
codeEvidence.explanation: An arbitrary family outside the installed catalogue can resolve to the same valid font part as other aliases; each is independently copied and stored.

rootCause.summary: `parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.

findings.remediation: Cache decoded font buffers by resolved package part and effective obfuscation key, share Arc values across aliases, and enforce an aggregate decoded-font allocation/work budget before copying.

counterEvidence: Known catalogue families are skipped; use distinct unknown names.
Invalid fonts are skipped; a single valid embedded font is sufficient.
The map stores Arc values, but each iteration creates new data and a fresh Arc; there is no source-part sharing here.
ZIP byte and XML depth/attribute limits do not charge multiplicity of font aliases.
limitations: Static validation only; no exploit document or measured allocation threshold.
validation.summary: A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.

dataflow.summary: Admitted fontTable XML -> unique FontEntry names -> same embedded part -> repeated deobfuscate_odttf copies -> retained EmbeddedFonts

likelihood.why: Valid small aliases to one ordinary font reach the eager loader under default options.

reachability.summary: Default public document rendering loads all embedded fonts before body run selection, so the supplier needs no operator-controlled configuration.

attackPath.summary: Supply a small DOCX with one valid embedded font and many unique unknown font-table aliases referencing it; invoke normal PDF/PNG/render conversion.

remediationTests: Load many unique aliases referencing one valid embedded part and assert shared buffers and bounded aggregate allocation.
Exercise distinct effective font keys and malformed fonts without bypassing aggregate budgets.

findings.title: Rendering short WMF records can allocate gigabytes from overlapping text
findings.summary: The WMF parser checks declared record sizes against the file but reads text and point payloads from the entire file. Many tiny text records can each copy the same following 65,535 bytes into retained strings, exhausting memory from a small admitted DOCX image.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can trigger large allocation and replay amplification through supported embedded WMF rendering under ordinary API options. Impact is availability of the calling process; Rust slice checks prevent out-of-buffer disclosure and no remote deployment was assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A shared externally exposed converter increases availability impact; isolated resource-limited workers reduce blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Parent inspection confirms whole-file string reads, record-size-only cursor advancement and retained MetaText allocations. No runtime allocation threshold was measured.

codeEvidence.label: Renderer forwards embedded metafile bytes before raster decoding
codeEvidence.explanation: Package image bytes enter the custom WMF parser and retain returned text.

codeEvidence.label: Record length bounds traversal only
codeEvidence.explanation: Each record size is checked against remaining file, then fields are read from whole data rather than a record slice.

codeEvidence.label: Text count escapes current record extent
codeEvidence.explanation: Both text operations validate string bytes against whole-file length instead of off+size2 and append the decoded copy.

codeEvidence.label: Text survives in MetaText
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected cross-record bytes are allocated as a new String and retained for each text record.

codeEvidence.label: Traversal advances only declared record size
codeEvidence.explanation: Short declared records advance a few bytes while each may copy a 65535-byte suffix.

codeEvidence.label: Untrusted WMF magic dispatch
codeEvidence.explanation: The image decoder selects WMF solely from bytes and sends it to raster_wmf.

rootCause.summary: `decode_image()` routes embedded WMF bytes into `raster_wmf()`. The parser validates only that `size2` fits the remaining file; handlers still receive the entire `data` buffer. `EXTTEXTOUT` and `TEXTOUT` use attacker counts in whole-file slices without requiring those slices to fit the current record. `wmf_text()` allocates a String for each such slice, and `texts` retains it while the cursor advances by only the small declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline handlers likewise read geometry beyond record-local extents, multiplying replay work.

findings.remediation: Slice every WMF record to its declared extent and make all field, string, font and point reads relative to that slice. Reject inconsistent lengths before copying/replay and enforce aggregate text/geometry work budgets.

counterEvidence: Canvas dimensions are capped at 384 per side and hostile coordinates are clipped; these controls do not bound retained strings.
Record size must be at least three words and the cursor advances, preventing a zero-length infinite loop.
Whole-file Rust slice bounds avoid arbitrary memory reads; the finding concerns invalid record extents and resource amplification.
ZIP admission charges original media bytes rather than repeated decoding of overlapping record suffixes.
limitations: Source-derived construction only; no application, payload or memory measurement executed.
validation.summary: A placeable WMF with nonzero bounds can use 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT records containing y/x/count/options but no local text bytes. With count 65535 and options zero, each handler reads subsequent records as text when enough file bytes remain. Tens of thousands of records in roughly 1 MB therefore retain several GB of overlapping decoded text. Header fields remain in bounds and each nonempty string is retained before traversal continues.

dataflow.summary: DOCX image part -> decode_image() -> metafile::render() -> short WMF record -> whole-file text slice -> retained MetaText String
dataflow.sink: Repeated text allocations and geometry replay

impact.why: Allocation and replay exhaustion of renderer.

likelihood.why: Tiny record extents and large valid whole-file counts directly reach retained allocation.

reachability.entrypoint: Public document rendering with referenced WMF media

attackPath.summary: Embed a referenced placeable WMF with many short EXTTEXTOUT records claiming long following strings in an otherwise admitted DOCX, then invoke ordinary rendering.

remediationTests: Reject EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT strings extending into the next record.
Reject cross-record polygon/polypolygon/polyline coordinates and validate large valid records within aggregate text/geometry budgets.

findings.title: Redacting visible text can leave a recoverable UTF-16 XML copy
findings.summary: A body redaction can succeed while the same sensitive text survives in an untouched UTF-16 auxiliary XML part. The package accepts and preserves that encoding, but the final leak check treats XML as UTF-8 and misses the retained copy.

severity.rationale: The protection is specifically intended to prevent disclosure when redacted outputs are shared. A recipient can recover the retained text from auxiliary XML, but this requires an existing duplicate in supported UTF-16 XML and subsequent sharing; no automatic external transmission is asserted.
severity.changeConditions: Evidence of routine redaction of highly sensitive duplicated data would increase impact; independent output sanitization or withholding the file removes the disclosure path.

confidence.rationale: Parent source review verifies UTF-16 admission, byte-preserving auxiliary output, UTF-8-only XML scanning and the final gate that trusts no matches. No application reproduction was run.

codeEvidence.label: Documented redaction confidentiality promise
codeEvidence.code:
Replace the unique occurrence of ``find`` (or its ``occurrence``-th hit) with one block per character.

The redaction is no tracked change: the clean copy and the redline
both show the blocks. The plan is refused with ``REDACTION_LEAK``
when the text still occurs anywhere in either document (another
paragraph, a comment, a header, the properties); the report never

codeEvidence.explanation: The promised REDACTION_LEAK refusal applies when target text remains anywhere in either output.

codeEvidence.label: XML fallback cannot reconstruct UTF-16
codeEvidence.explanation: The fallback searches the same lossy UTF-8 string, which retains interleaved NULs rather than the decoded target.

rootCause.summary: Admission decodes BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE XML for validation, so a `customXml/item1.xml` holding the target text is supported input. Redaction rewrites the body and touched stories, preserving untouched part bytes in the clean DOCX. `check_redactions()` scans generated outputs through `scrub::leaks()`, but its XML branch passes lossy UTF-8 to `xml_holds()` instead of decoding the XML encoding. Interleaved UTF-16 NULs prevent semantic or fallback matching; the raw UTF-16 needle check is available only to non-XML parts. An empty match set permits successful return with the sensitive bytes still present.

findings.remediation: Reuse a BOM/encoding-aware XML decoder before leak scanning, handling UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE, and fail closed when an XML part cannot be decoded or scanned completely.

counterEvidence: Archive read/inflation failures fail closed and UTF-8 XML comments, processing instructions/entities and joined Word runs are scanned.
Neither those controls nor the non-XML UTF-16LE fallback covers UTF-16 XML.
A simple transitional package does not need strict translation that could rewrite auxiliary XML.
limitations: Static source validation only; disclosure additionally requires sharing the returned document with a recipient.
validation.summary: Use ordinary transitional body XML containing a multi-character target and an auxiliary BOM-marked UTF-16 XML element containing the same target. Admission supports both endiannesses; untouched auxiliary bytes serialize verbatim. The XML branch searches a NUL-interleaved UTF-8 interpretation rather than the decoded target, so it yields no auxiliary hit after visible redaction.

Replace the unique occurrence of ``find`` (or its ``occurrence``-th hit) with one block per character.

The redaction is no tracked change: the clean copy and the redline

rootCause.summary: `check_redactions()` refuses outputs only when `scrub::leaks()` finds the target. For XML attributes, `xml_holds()` ignores a matching value if its local name appears in `NUMERIC_ATTRIBUTES` and its value is hexadecimal-looking. The exemption checks neither namespace nor owning element/part. Thus business XML `<customer id="123456789"/>`, including a business-namespaced `id`, is treated like an OOXML layout identifier. Ordinary body redaction leaves that auxiliary part unchanged and the final scan reports no residual target.

findings.remediation: Remove numeric exemptions from strict redaction verification, or restrict them to verified OOXML namespace/element/attribute combinations representing exclusively generated layout state. Always scan arbitrary custom XML business attributes.

counterEvidence: Exempting genuine OOXML dimensions/generated IDs avoids unrelated short numeric matches and is covered by existing tests.
That purpose does not establish arbitrary custom XML business identifiers as safe; the code does not constrain namespace/element/part.
Nonnumeric attribute values are scanned normally.
limitations: No dynamic integration reproduction; disclosure additionally requires sharing the returned DOCX.
validation.summary: A custom XML attribute with `id=123456789` reaches the matching-value branch, passes `is_number()`, and is skipped solely because local_name is id. No other text node need contain the identifier after body redaction. The retained custom part is serialized verbatim; the check then permits the result.

Retain explicit tests for legitimate OOXML layout exemptions only if their exact namespace and element contexts are enforced.

originalCandidate.title: Numeric custom XML values bypass redaction leak checking
originalCandidate.originalMessage: Same redaction checker has second independent static false-negative: xml_holds at scrub.rs:539-578 skips NUMERIC_ATTRIBUTES by name.local_name() and is_number(value), regardless of namespace/part. Untouched business customXml <customer id="123456789"/> or <record x:id="123456789" xmlns:x="urn:business"/> is skipped after visible account/identifier 123456789 is redacted from body. Numeric identifier copies in arbitrary custom XML are actual sensitive data, unlike OOXML layout IDs. This needs restricting exemptions to exact OOXML namespace+element/attribute contexts (or removing them in strict redaction scans). Deliberate tests exempt layout numeric values, but do not cover unrelated customXml namespace collisions.

threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a Rust Word-document toolkit exposed as native CLI, Rust byte APIs, Python/PyO3 facade and stdio MCP server, and browser/Node WASM APIs plus npm CLI. Documents and edit plans pass through admission/XML/package processing to DOCX, Markdown, PDF/PNG and reports. Normal processing is local; explicit native self-update downloads and installs a GitHub release (src/lib.rs:7-35,96-165; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; src/update.rs:186-258).
assets: Confidential document bytes, revisions/comments/authors and derived renderings/reports; integrity of selected input/output files and admitted package structures (src/lib.rs:17-30; src/publication.rs:146-225).
MCP root filesystem capability; native executable integrity on self-update; release publishing/signing authority (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-275,356-369; src/update.rs:25-48,198-258).

Native renderers read installed/user/Word cloud-cache fonts and persist a per-user font index, distinct from document output-root authority (src/convert/font.rs:2228-2236,2633-2652,3090-3107,3213-3227).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted DOCX/ZIP/XML, legacy DOC, embedded images/fonts and edit plans enter the engine. Default admission bounds archive/part bytes 64 MiB, 10000 entries, inflation 256 MiB, XML depth 256; comparison allows 512 MiB archive/part and 2 GiB inflation. Permissive parse_xdocument requires a prior gate (src/admission.rs:15-28,63-99; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-36).

MCP stdio client invokes document tools under operator --root (default cwd). Python resolves paths for diagnostics; native _OutputRoot owns confined reads/publication through a held capability. Annotations are hints, not caller authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1277; src/publication.rs:146-199).

Native CLI grants ambient paths with staged per-file publication. Python/Node CLI ambient reads/writes are separate from MCP confinement (src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:203-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:142-145; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-132; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-56,106-110).

Native Markdown images use --resource-path or Markdown parent directory; URL schemes/canonical escape targets are refused, followed by capability-relative read (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2876,2936-2943).

Self-update enters executable replacement only on explicit command and confirmation/--yes. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean checksum-only today; optional Ed25519 support is inactive (src/update.rs:25-48,120-125,198-258,274-285; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82).

Tag-triggered release builds are read-only; release job has contents:write, signing step receives signing secret and publishes dist/* with workflow token. These are CI/maintainer authorities (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-55,230-275,356-369).
attackerCapabilities: Document suppliers control package/XML/relationship/font/image/Markdown bytes, not operator environment, MCP root grants or release infrastructure (src/admission.rs:15-28; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2876).

Authorized MCP clients read/publish inside granted root including explicit overwrite; tools do not grant updater or ambient path authority (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,153-217,373-381).

Control of release assets permits changing archive and adjacent checksum; this is a separate supply-chain starting capability not authenticated by checksum-only policy (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-77; src/update.rs:44-48,245-248).
securityObjectives: Do not fetch external document relationships or Markdown URL resources; confine MCP and resource reads to granted directory capabilities (src/admission.rs:15-22; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2876; src/publication.rs:146-199).
Refuse malformed/over-budget packages/XML before DOM processing; host memory/CPU process bounds remain necessary (src/admission.rs:39-99; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-36; SECURITY.md:70-85).
Bind source_sha256 to document bytes when supplied and reject stale plans; staged publication is atomic per file only (src/edit.rs:2081-2089; src/publication.rs:83-131,168-174).

Protect updater integrity with HTTPS/checksums, configured signatures and regular-file check; keep document processing distinct from release publication (src/update.rs:198-258,299-307; .github/workflows/release.yml:230-275).
assumptions: No deployment, tenants or HTTP listener supplied; MCP uses stdio and operator controls client attachment/root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381).

Limits are configurable; hosts should not silently raise them for hostile inputs. Low-level permissive XML APIs require prior checking (src/admission.rs:103-164; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:21-30; SECURITY.md:70-85).
Updater docs disclose checksum-only operation until a key is committed; signature support is not active authentication (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-82; src/update.rs:44-48).

Overview says no temporary files, but native font lookup persists an index and PID temporary sibling: a documentation qualification, not demonstrated vulnerability (src/lib.rs:7-11; src/convert/font.rs:3098-3107,3213-3227).
Current source audit only, no Git history or runtime execution; architecture mapping does not establish full audit coverage.
